sections.h2: Where is Worcester County, Maryland, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Worcester County is Maryland's only county on the Atlantic Ocean, in the far southeast corner of the state, and Snow Hill is the county seat. Wikipedia lists 695 square miles in total, 468 of them land, which makes it the second-largest Maryland county by total area. It is also the only one bordering both Delaware and Virginia.

The county was created in 1742 from Somerset County. The ground is flat and low, and the high point is only 49 feet, in the northwest near Route 12. Barrier islands, Fenwick and Assateague, shelter the coast. The Pocomoke River and its swamp run through the south.

The 2020 census counted 52,460 residents, with a median age of about 50.5. Towns include Ocean City, Berlin, Snow Hill and Pocomoke City, plus Ocean Pines, which is a census-designated place rather than a town.

sections.h2: How does Ocean City change the Worcester County housing picture?
sections.html:
Ocean City makes Worcester County unusual, because most of its homes are used seasonally. The 2020 census counted 30,028 housing units there and only 3,820 occupied year-round, with about 87 percent vacant, mostly seasonal use, according to the Ocean City article.

The resort sits on a barrier spit about 9 miles long and about 6.6 feet above sea level. Year-round population was 6,844 in 2020, but summer weekends bring 320,000 or more people. Condominium building boomed in the 1970s, with more than 15,000 units added.

For a seller, that matters because many Worcester County properties are second homes, rentals or inherited units, and each of those has its own tax and closing timeline.

  • Owners who live elsewhere still owe the bill, and a missing mailed bill is not an excuse.
  • Heirs of a beach unit need a payoff figure before they can list.
  • Rental owners should confirm who holds the tax bill at settlement.

sections.h2: What does the economy look like outside the resort?
sections.html:
Inland Worcester County runs on farming, poultry and small-town trades. Agriculture, seafood, timber and truck farming were the historic base, and large-scale poultry became a major industry after mid-century.

Pocomoke City grew around logging, shingle making and shipbuilding on the river. Berlin sits near the birthplace of naval officer Stephen Decatur. Public schools are run by Worcester County Public Schools, with Stephen Decatur, Snow Hill, Pocomoke and Worcester Technical high schools. Shore Transit and Ocean City's beach bus carry riders, and the nearest commercial airport is Salisbury-Ocean City-Wicomico Regional.

The 1962 Ash Wednesday nor'easter destroyed much of the residential development on Assateague Island and led to the national seashore and state park there.

sections.h2: Which office collects Worcester County property tax?
sections.html:
The Worcester County Treasurer's Office collects the bill, and the state assessment office sets the value. The Treasurer is at the Government Center, 1 West Market Street, Room 1105, Snow Hill, MD 21863, and also has a second location at the Isle of Wight Center, 13070 St. Martins Neck Road, Bishopville.

Bills are available online through the Taxes Online link on the county's real property tax page. In July 2026 the county told owners who had not received a mailed bill to look it up online instead of waiting.

sections.h2: What are the Worcester County property tax rates?
sections.html:
Worcester County lists a county rate of $0.815 per $100 of assessed value, plus the state rate of $0.112, and a separate town rate where one applies. The county's real property page gives these town rates.

The county collects Ocean City's tax for the town. The page is not dated, so confirm the current rates with the Treasurer before you rely on them.

sections.h2: When are Worcester County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Annual bills go out in July and become delinquent on October 1, after which interest runs at 1 percent per month. Bills for the 2026 to 2027 tax year were made available online starting July 1, 2026, and printed bills were mailed the week of July 6.

Paying the County tax in full in July earns a 0.5 percent discount. Principal residences, and businesses with taxes up to $100,000, can pay twice a year. The first installment is delinquent October 1, the second is due December 1, and interest starts January 1. A six-month bill for new construction is mailed each January.

One rule catches people out. The county says a payment must be received by the Treasurer by the last day of the month, and postmarks are not accepted.

  • July: bills issued, 0.5 percent discount on County tax.
  • October 1: unpaid annual bills and first installments go delinquent.
  • October 1: deadline to apply for the Homeowner's Tax Credit.
  • January 1: interest begins on a late second installment.

sections.h2: How do assessments and appeals work in Worcester County?
sections.html:
The state Department of Assessments and Taxation reassesses property every three years, and owners get a notice with the old and new value. SDAT's January 2026 report lists a residential value change of 10.5 percent for Worcester County, and notices were mailed December 30, 2025. Increases are phased in over three years.

You have 45 days from the notice date to appeal. The first step is an informal review with an assessor. The second is the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, which needs a filing within 30 days of the supervisor's final notice. The third is the Maryland Tax Court, again within 30 days of the board order. If you buy between January 1 and July 1, you have 60 days from the transfer, after the deed is recorded. See the SDAT appeal page.

Owners may also qualify for credits. The Homeowner's Tax Credit depends on income and must be requested each year by October 1, and the county's Homestead Tax Credit appears automatically when an owner-occupied assessment rises past the set percentage.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Worcester County taxes?
sections.html:
Worcester County holds an annual tax sale of properties with unpaid taxes, and not receiving a bill is no excuse. The 2026 sale was set for June 9, according to the state schedule, and earlier sales were May 16, 2025 and May 17, 2024.

State law makes unpaid real property tax a lien from the due date until paid. An owner who falls behind should call the Treasurer's Office early, because interest keeps running at 1 percent per month until the bill is paid.

sections.h2: What transfer and recordation costs apply when selling in Worcester County?
sections.html:
A Worcester County sale carries a state transfer tax, a county transfer tax and a recordation tax. A Maryland law firm summary lists the recordation tax at 0.66 percent, the county transfer tax at 0.5 percent and the state transfer tax at 0.5 percent, for 1.66 percent on deeds. The first $50,000 of the county transfer tax is exempt if the buyer will live in the home at least 7 months of the year.

Since January 1, 2025, the Treasurer collects recordation tax for documents submitted after December 31, 2024, with checks payable to Worcester County. Questions go to 410-632-0686, option 3. Rates change, so have the title company confirm the figures before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: When are Worcester County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Annual bills are mailed in July and become delinquent October 1, with interest at 1 percent per month after that. Owners who qualify for two payments have a first installment delinquent October 1 and a second due December 1.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Worcester County taxes early?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the County tax in full during July earns a 0.5 percent discount on the County portion.

faqs.q: Where is the Worcester County Treasurer's Office?
faqs.a: The main office is at 1 West Market Street, Room 1105, in Snow Hill, and a second office is at the Isle of Wight Center in Bishopville. Both are open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Does the county collect Ocean City property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Worcester County collects Ocean City's real property tax at $0.4326 per $100 of assessed value, according to the county's tax page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Worcester County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax is a lien, so the payoff is normally taken from the sale proceeds at settlement. Ask the Treasurer for a current payoff before you set a closing date.
